BagClust1 for shape clustering

Source: R/bagclust1.R
bagclust1.Rd

Each bootstrap replicate fits the base clusterer to a resample and then assigns every one of the n original observations to its nearest bootstrap medoid or center, so all observations vote in every replicate (Dudoit and Fridlyand, 2003, BagClust1).

Usage

bagclust1(
  Z,
  K,
  base = c("pam", "rankkmed", "kmeans", "clarans", "hill"),
  B = 100L,
  distance = c("rho", "dF", "dP"),
  seed = NULL,
  parallel = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  reflection = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

Z

Either a complex pre-shape matrix of size (k-1) x n (2D shapes, from landmarks_to_preshape), or a real landmark array of dimension k x m x n with m = 2 or 3. Base clusterer "kmeans" needs the real array.

K

Number of clusters.

base

Base clusterer. One of "pam" (default), "rankkmed", "kmeans" (shape_kmeans), "clarans" (shape_clarans) or "hill" (shape_hill). The first, second, fourth and fifth fit on the distance matrix of the resample and label observations by the nearest medoid; "kmeans" fits on the landmarks of the resample and labels observations by the nearest center (mean shape).

B

Number of bootstrap replicates (default 100).

distance

One of "rho" (default), "dF" or "dP" ("dP", the partial Procrustes distance, is new in the development version). It builds the distance matrix the medoid methods work on and the distance to the centers of "kmeans".

seed

Optional integer seed. The result is then reproducible and identical with and without parallel; the caller's random-number stream is left as it was.

parallel

Logical. If TRUE, use parallel::mclapply (Unix/macOS) or parallel::parLapply (Windows).

n_cores

Number of cores to use if parallel = TRUE. Default = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1).

reflection

Logical, for real landmark arrays only: if TRUE, reflections are removed too (see shape_distance). Not available for base = "kmeans".

...

Additional arguments passed to the base clusterer (e.g., m = 7 for rankkmed, mean = "phi" for kmeans, numlocal and maxneighbor for clarans, max_iter for hill).

Value

A list of class "bagclust1" with components:

cluster

Integer vector of length n, the majority-vote consensus labels.

votes

n x K integer matrix of vote counts (rows sum to B).

reference

Integer vector, the reference (non-bagged) clustering used for label alignment.

B

Number of bootstrap replicates.

base

Base clusterer name.

References

Dudoit, S. and Fridlyand, J. (2003). Bagging to improve the accuracy of a clustering procedure. Bioinformatics, 19(9), 1090–1099. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btg038

Examples

set.seed(1)
k <- 4; n <- 60
# 3 clusters via mean shift
X <- array(0, dim = c(k, 2, n))
for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  g <- ((i - 1) %% 3) + 1
  mu <- matrix(c(0,0, 1,0, 0,1, 1,1), 4, 2, byrow = TRUE)
  X[,,i] <- mu + matrix(rnorm(k*2, sd = 0.1 * g), k, 2)
}
Z <- landmarks_to_preshape(X)
fit <- bagclust1(Z, K = 3, base = "pam", B = 30, seed = 1)
table(fit$cluster)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#>  9 20 31 

# 3D shapes: a real k x 3 x n array, here with the k-means base clusterer
sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 10, sigma = 0.5, seed = 1)
fit3 <- bagclust1(sim$X, K = 2, base = "kmeans", B = 10, seed = 1)
table(fit3$cluster, sim$group)
#>    
#>      1  2
#>   1  0 10
#>   2 10  0
